newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MAPLE LEAFS FIRE GM CLIFF FLETCHER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MAPLE LEAFS FIRE GM CLIFF FLETCHER.

text.p: The Toronto Maple Leafs, who finished last in the NHL Central Division this season, Saturday fired General Manager Cliff Fletcher after six years of guiding the team's up and down fortunes.
Assistant GM Bill Watters will serve as interim general manager until a replacement is hired, Leafs Chairman Steve Stavro announced.
Fletcher, who has been a general manager in the National Hockey League for the past 25 years, guided the Maple Leafs to the conference finals in 1993 and 1994.
But the team, which has not won the Stanley Cup since 1967, has fallen back on hard times and never seemed in position to make a run at a playoff spot this season.
When his core of veteran players failed to get the job done, Fletcher reversed strategy and tried to salvage the season by trading Doug Gilmour and Kirk Muller in favour of a youth movement.
The move could not save the season or Fletcher's job as Toronto finished with a 30-44-8 record and missed the playoffs for the first time since 1992.
"This has been an amicable resolution and I wish the Maple Leafs every success in the future," Fletcher said. "I must say that I have really enjoyed my six years at Maple Leaf Gardens."

Prior to taking the Toronto post, Fletcher was the Calgary Flames general manager for the first 19 years of the team's existence. He helped organise the club's move from Atlanta to Calgary and built the Flames into Stanley Cup champions in 1989.
